messages:
maya: quick sync: follow-up to the adaptive-credit dampener RFC. i think we need a clearer separation between admission math and abuse advisories so we don't couple rollout paths.

devin: agree. proposal: admission returns (allowed_tokens, lease_ms, spill_to_best_effort) and a versioned admission_id. abuse service returns a lightweight advisory: multiplier (0..1), hold_ms, tags. admission applies advisory.

lee: minimal signals list is necessary: last_1m_rps, last_5m_error_rate, p95_lat_ms, burst_count_1m. keep payload tiny to preserve hot path.

samira: also require advisory metadata: api_version, model_hash, computed_at, and a signature or monotonic counter so admission can detect stale advice.

jon: rollout plan: two-phase canary. phase A read-only (advice logged but ignored). phase B apply behind feature flag. track metrics: advice_total, advice_applied, advice_mismatch_count, downstream_5m_sla_delta.

maya: fallback behavior? if abuse times out, default multiplier=1.0 unless tenant_profile.emergency_policy == "fail_closed". ops can flip manual_quarantine via admin endpoint.

devin: implementation note: abuse eval must be idempotent and cheaply computable; heavy ML scoring only in async pipeline that writes back a cached advisory. realtime eval should be rules + lightweight heuristics.

samira: security: only the admission service may call /abuse/eval via mTLS; audit events for manual_quarantine toggles.

ops-bot: reminder: deploy window tomorrow 09:00 UTC for branch/devin/advice-shim.

maya: ok next steps: samira drafts formal contract + signal set; devin builds shim; lee prepares canary dashboard. i'll add product for default policies. thanks all.
